svg.title: iOS · Capture — Interval (running, scheduled peek) · portrait
svg.desc:
Mirrors App/CaptureView.swift + App/ShootScreenDimmer.swift — the card a scheduled peek lifts the blackout to show. Settings ▸ Display ▸ Scheduled peek (settings.display.portrait.svg), on by default, every 5 minutes on the wall clock.
WHY A CARD AND NOT THE VIEWFINDER. The peek exists to answer "is this shoot going well?" from wherever the operator is standing, without a finger on a phone that is on a tripod. A restored live viewfinder answers that badly: at three metres it says the screen is on and nothing else. This card is legible at that distance, and it is also CHEAPER than the viewfinder it replaces — around 94% of the panel stays black, so an OLED phone pays almost nothing for the fifteen seconds, which is what makes a peek affordable on a device that turned the blackout on for thermal reasons in the first place. The blackout is not lifted underneath: the card is drawn on the same black, and brightness is restored to the device level, or to the reduced level when Settings ▸ Display ▸ Reduce brightness is on.
READING ORDER, top to bottom, in the order the operator's questions arrive. (1) The latest frame, 160×120, so "check the shots" is literally answered — this is the one thing a counter cannot tell you, and the caption dates it. (2) The frame count as the hero, in the rounded tabular face the standby countdown uses (capture-standby.portrait.svg — the two screens are deliberately siblings, one before the run and one during it). (3) The health line, which is the verdict: green dot + "On schedule" while the delivered cadence tracks the request; it turns amber + "Falling behind" when it does not, which is the honest reading of a starved window. (4) Three chips in the standby card's shape and geometry — ELAPSED, THERMAL, SPACE. A chip whose value has gone wrong colours its VALUE only, leaving the label grey: thermal serious in #FF9F0A, critical in #FF3B30, and space under an hour of headroom likewise. (5) The exposure line, verbatim the amber string the running readout carries (runExposureLine), so the peek and the live screen never disagree. (6) The blend line, the short form of blendDiagnosticsReadout.
THE FOOTER IS PART OF THE FEATURE. The bar and its countdown say the blackout is coming back on purpose — a screen that goes black on its own with no warning reads as a crash, and this run has two hours left. "next peek 3:20" is the line that means the operator never has to touch the phone at all: it names when they can look again. A tap anywhere hands over the real screen for 30 s (ShootScreenDimmer.wake), which is the existing escape and the only route to the stop control; the card itself carries no controls, deliberately — a shutter-sized target on a screen you are meant to glance at is how a tripod gets nudged.
Sample data is one run: 41 minutes into a 3s interval, blend 3, DNG, nominal. The alert form of the card (falling behind, thermal serious) is listed in INDEX.md rather than drawn. The layout is centred within a max width so it reflows in landscape without a bespoke file.

g.text: Screen returns in 12 s · next peek 3:20
